notes.body: When reviewing, please pay attention to this change. It looks good to me, but please double check.
as retransmission_timer is a guint32, the previous code seemed correct to me (now you are comparing a double against a guint32)
That resulted in a compiler warning, since there is no straight conversion from double to guint32.

```
../epan/dissectors/packet-dns.c: In function ‘dissect_dns_common’:
../epan/dissectors/packet-dns.c:4142:13: warning: cast from function call of type ‘double’ to non-matching type ‘unsigned int’ [-Wbad-function-cast]
 4142 |         if ((guint32)nstime_to_sec(&request_delta) < retransmission_timer) {
```
So if you cast `retransmission_timer` as double, what happens?
Good point. It seems to please the compiler. Update on the run.

If more casts are required, it does not necessarily make sense. Without knowing what are the warnings that you are trying to fix as they do not appear with my compiler, I can only make guess based on the changes and this one seemed surprising.

All the warnings in this section are related to signedness. The is no way to choose a type that doesn't require cast: for instance `format_text()` requires a guchar and returns a gchar. I tried to guess which one would have resulted in less casts.

I'm using `gcc (Ubuntu 9.3.0-17ubuntu1~20.04) 9.3.0`.

Warnings appear in the MR job merge-req:ubuntu-gcc-ctest

https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/jobs/941328193
